newsitem.title: ROMANIA: TROUBLED ROMANIAN BANK'S FATE DUE IN TWO WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: TROUBLED ROMANIAN BANK'S FATE DUE IN TWO WEEKS.

text.p: A Romanian court is expected to rule within the next two weeks on whether to approve a recovery plan of the troubled Dacia Felix SA private bank or liquidate it, court sources said on Tuesday.

"After I have collected opinions from experts I will make a decision on (the bank's) recovery plan," judge Ioan Georgiu told a news conference in the Transylvanian city of Cluj, where Dacia Felix is based.
"I estimate it will take me about two weeks to gather those opinions," Georgiu added.
Under the law, if the court rejects Dacia Felix's recovery plan, the bank faces liquidation.
Dacia Felix had been in trouble for months after revealing over $200 million worth of bad debts and a 642.2 billion lei 1995 loss. Dacia owes creditors some 2.3 trillion lei.
Late last week its board submitted to court a recovery programme which includes repayment of creditors as well as a rise in the bank's share capital.
"I have to call a meeting of creditors before ruling on the recovery plan," Georgiu said.

In July, the central bank -- the main creditor of Dacia Felix -- asked the Cluj court to decide on the fate of the bank after it neared financial collapse. So far it has not withdrawn Dacia Felix's banking licence.

Dacia Felix's major debtors are companies associated with its figurehead, former tennis player Sever Muresan, and the Grupul Darianne holding. Muresan-led companies owed Dacia 1.17 trillion lei, of which 453 billion lei was interest repayments, while Darianne's debt amounted to 146 billion lei.
On Tuesday, Romania's upper house of Senate empowered the central bank to give credits to Dacia Felix to help small depositors redeem their money. ($=3,261 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
